title: object_put_converges_on_remote_target fails ~8% of runs with EADDRINUSE: fake target binds a hardcoded port
failure_signature:
thread 'object_put_converges_on_remote_target' panicked at crates/e2e_test/src/replication_target_matrix_test.rs:212:14:
  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Address already in use (os error 98)
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
The failure is always at mock-target bind, never at the convergence assertion.

error_decode.meaning: EADDRINUSE - the address is already in use. Linux value 98; the macOS value is 48, so the number is resolved on the host that failed.
error_decode.source: python3 -c 'import os; print(os.strerror(98))' on the Linux runner; /usr/include/asm-generic/errno-base.h
error_decode.emitted_by: crates/e2e_test/src/replication_target_matrix_test.rs:212 - start_fake_target's listener bind, which unwraps the TcpListener::bind result

error_decode.meaning: The unwrap is at the fixture's bind, so the failure is in setup rather than in the replication logic the test exists to check.
error_decode.source: RUST_BACKTRACE=1 run of the failing iteration
error_decode.emitted_by: same line; backtrace confirms no frames below the fixture's own bind

symptom_summary: Fails roughly 8% of runs with EADDRINUSE while binding the fake replication target, and only when the sibling test in the same module also runs. Passes 50/50 when run alone.
root_cause: The fake replication target binds a hardcoded port (9411) instead of an ephemeral one, and two tests in the same module bind it concurrently. Under process-per-test execution their lifetimes overlap, so whichever loses the bind panics at setup. The convergence logic under test is never reached on a failing run, so the failure signature is misleading: it looks like a replication bug and is a fixture collision.

discrimination.implication: The test is internally deterministic. Eliminates async scheduling, wall-clock timing, orphan-task, and cancellation-safety families as the cause of the observed failure.

discrimination.outcome: Full suite passed with no failures across 5 iterations.
discrimination.implication: The failure requires concurrency. Narrowing to resource contention or global-state mutation, and away from anything intrinsic to the test body.

discrimination.outcome: 7 failures in 20 iterations, all EADDRINUSE, all in the put test.
discrimination.implication: The failure follows the sibling test. Confirms a shared-resource collision between two specific tests rather than a general parallelism problem, and rules out order dependence in the sense of leaked state (nothing is left behind; the resource is held concurrently).

discrimination.command: applied fix: bind 127.0.0.1:0 and read back listener.local_addr(); then re-ran the same 20-iteration pair
discrimination.outcome: 20 iterations, 0 failures. Reverting to port 9411 reproduced 6 failures in 20.
discrimination.implication: Directly confirms the hardcoded port as the cause, in both directions.
Load was not needed to reproduce; the failure rate at rest was already 8%, well above the noise floor. Recorded as unverified rather than assumed.

confirming_experiment.hypothesis: If the hardcoded port 9411 is the cause, then binding an ephemeral port removes the failure and restoring the hardcoded port brings it back.
confirming_experiment.experiment: Patched the fake target fixture to bind 127.0.0.1:0 and pass listener.local_addr() to the client, ran the failing pair for 20 iterations, then reverted the patch and ran the same pair for 20 iterations.
confirming_experiment.result: Patched: 0 failures in 20. Reverted: 6 failures in 20, all EADDRINUSE at the same line. Both directions observed.

policy_context.violates_written_rule: docs/testing/README.md requires per-test random ports and isolated temp dirs; this fixture uses a fixed port.
constraints_on_fix: Must not add the test to a max-threads = 1 test group, since the project rule is isolation over serialization and the fix is two lines.
The outbound target matrix expectation table in docs pins known-red cells to an open issue; the fixed port is not one of those cells, so no expectation-table change is needed.

proposed_fix.summary: Bind the fake replication target to an ephemeral port and read the assigned address back, instead of hardcoding 9411.
rejected_alternatives: Add retries=2 for this test. Rejected: the project flake policy requires a linked open issue and a fix-or-delete deadline, and this is a two-line fix with a confirmed cause.
Add a [test-groups] entry with max-threads = 1. Rejected: slower, and it leaves the collision in place for anyone who adds a third sibling later.
Widen the mock target startup timeout. Rejected: the failure is a bind error, not a timeout, so no timeout change affects it.
proposed_fix.expected_effect: Flake rate at 50 iterations goes from 8% to 0%. Predicted from the confirming experiment, not yet measured on the full pair plus the rest of the module.

blast_radius: delete_marker_replication in the same module binds the same port and is the observed collision partner.
Any future test in replication_target_matrix_test that calls start_fake_target inherits the same collision, so the fix removes a recurring class rather than one instance.
not_verified: The fix was not applied, so the 0% rate is predicted from the two-direction experiment rather than measured on a full 50-iteration run of the patched module.
Not tested on macOS or ARM; the CI lane is Linux-only.
Did not check whether other e2e modules hardcode ports, so the blast radius outside this module is unquantified.
Did not run the load axis, so it is unconfirmed whether the rate also rises under CPU pressure.
Did not verify the claim about the project's quarantine policy against .config/nextest.toml; it comes from docs/testing/README.md.
suggested_next_step: Apply the two-line port fix, run the full module for 50 iterations to confirm 0%, then open an issue referencing FLAKY-001 and attach the stress output as evidence.
tooling_gaps: tokio-console was not installed, so had the failure turned out to be a hang rather than a bind error there would have been no task-level introspection available.
No nightly toolchain, so the shuffle-seed ordering sweep and ThreadSanitizer were unavailable; neither was needed here.
